title: Mitigate customer TTFT spikes and tokens/sec drop via emergency routing + KV prefetch rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Several paying customers across Hosted/Dedicated/Private surfaced production regressions: large increases in time-to-first-token (TTFT) and sudden drops in tokens/sec for interactive chat workloads after the recent kernel selection and KV cache heuristics rollout. Symptoms: 1) TTFT +1.5x on 8k+ context prompts for multimodal-ish models, 2) sustained tokens/sec throughput reduction (20-40%) for multiplexed routes under normal QPS, 3) disparity across variants (quantized vs fp16) and across regions. Impact: customer-facing SLA alerts and P1 escalations from three enterprise accounts. Initial triage indicates the kernel-selector optimization occasionally chooses a new execution path that disables aggressive KV prefetch for long contexts; that path is much more sensitive to packing patterns and causes serialization stalls in the request pipeline.

Goal: implement an emergency mitigation to restore baseline TTFT and throughput, stabilize affected customers, and plan a robust root-cause fix that preserves the intended performance win without regressions.

Scope: hosted API routes + dedicated pools + private VPC bundles. Must coordinate with SRE, Customer Success, and Security for private patches.
